quiz.0.question: Why is Primitivo called 'Primitivo'?
quiz.0.options.0: Because it produces very simple, 'primitive' wines
quiz.0.options.1: From 'primativo' — it ripens among the earliest of all Italian varieties
quiz.0.options.2: Because it was one of the first varieties planted in Italy
quiz.0.options.3: Because it was grown by primitive peoples
quiz.0.explanation: Primitivo comes from 'primativo' — meaning early-ripening. It is one of the earliest-ripening varieties in Italy, harvested in August in some areas.
quiz.1.question: What does the name Negroamaro mean?
quiz.1.options.1: 'Black' (nero) + 'bitter' (amaro) — describing the grape's deep colour and dry, bitter finish
quiz.1.explanation: Negroamaro literally means 'black-bitter': nero (Italian: black) for its deep, inky colour and amaro (Italian: bitter) for its characteristically dry, slightly bitter tannins.
quiz.2.question: What is the blend ratio for Cerasuolo di Vittoria DOCG?
quiz.2.explanation: Cerasuolo di Vittoria DOCG (Sicily's only DOCG) requires 50–70% Nero d'Avola blended with 30–50% Frappato — combining power with elegance.
quiz.3.question: Why did ancient Romans call Fiano 'Vitis Apiana'?
quiz.3.options.0: Because it originated in the Apennine mountains
quiz.3.options.1: Because bees (api) were irresistibly attracted to its sweet, ripe berries at harvest
quiz.3.options.2: Because it was the favourite wine of the god Apollo
quiz.3.options.3: Because it was cultivated in the Apia region
quiz.3.explanation: The Romans called Fiano 'Vitis Apiana' — 'the vine of bees' — because bees were irresistibly attracted to the intensely aromatic, honeyed berries. Fiano di Avellino DOCG is a direct descendant.
